item.title: Executing Court should execute decree without imposing onerous condition: Punjab and Haryana High Court
item.description: In the present case, the Executive Court imposed a condition directing the petitioner to furnish a bank guarantee for release of the amount. item.title: Punjab and Haryana HC: Transfer application cannot be allowed on whims or imaginary anxieties; clear evidence of genuine risk to fair trial required
item.description: “Judicial error is not synonymous with judicial partiality and hence mere passing of an unfavorable order, or even an order subsequently set aside by a superior Court, does not ipso facto establish a foundation for bias or prejudice.” The post Punjab and Haryana HC: Transfer application cannot be allowed on whims or imaginary anxieties; clear evidence of genuine risk to fair trial required appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: ‘Merely addressing the gathering’; Patna HC quashes assault case against Bihar Minister Santosh Kumar Suman
item.description: Upon perusal of the FIR and considering the submissions, the Court held that there was clearly no allegation of assault against Santosh Kumar and he was only addressing the gathering, which did not support the prosecution's case. The post ‘Merely addressing the gathering’; Patna HC quashes assault case against Bihar Minister Santosh Kumar Suman appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Inside Karnataka HC’s order upholding acquittal in POCSO case; highlights victim’s inconsistent and untrustworthy statements
item.description: The Court observed that the victim admitted being about 18 years old, while her father’s evidence on age was inconsistent. With contradictions between oral and medical evidence, minority was not proved, and hence, Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 could not be invoked. The post Inside Karnataka HC’s order upholding acquittal in POCSO case; highlights victim’s inconsistent and untrustworthy statements appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Examiner entitled to correct/re-evaluate marks “at the first blush”; Delhi HC dismisses plea challenging DJSE-2023 evaluation process
item.description: “In view of the express bar on re-evaluation, the subjective nature of the assessment, and the absence of any material error or exceptional circumstance, judicial interference is unwarranted.” The post Examiner entitled to correct/re-evaluate marks “at the first blush”; Delhi HC dismisses plea challenging DJSE-2023 evaluation process appeared first on SCC Times.
